 Taiwan exchange pledges to curb market turmoil after sharp selloff
 SECTIONS Taiwan exchange pledges to curb market turmoil after sharp selloff By Anupam Nagar , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 17, 2026, 11:12:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Taiwan's stock exchange has pledged to take measures to stabilise markets after a 6% slump in its benchmark index. The move comes amid heightened global volatility, AI sector concerns and jitters over the technology rally.

 ETMarkets.com Taiwan signals market support after 6% plunge as AI jitters rattle global equities. 
 Taiwan's stock exchange said it would take necessary measures to stabilise the market if sharp and prolonged declines or abnormal volatility persist, following a 6% slump in the benchmark index on Monday.
 The Taiwan Stock Exchange said it would coordinate with the relevant authorities and respond according to market conditions to ensure orderly trading and protect investors' interests. It did not specify what measures could be introduced.

According to Reuters, the exchange will continue to monitor international political and economic developments, strengthen market surveillance and risk management, and urge listed companies to promptly disclose material information.
It also advised investors to assess their risk tolerance carefully and remain cautious about margin financing and other leveraged trading amid heightened market volatility. Investors should focus on industry developments and corporate fundamentals rather than short-term market movements, it added.

 Despite recent turbulence in global financial markets, the exchange said international research institutions remained positive about the artificial intelligence industry's medium- and long-term prospects. Taiwan's exports and corporate operations have also continued to show strong growth momentum.
 Taiwan is highly dependent on exports and is home to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC), the world's largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to AI companies such as Nvidia.
Global markets have come under pressure following reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's resignation last week, adding to investor concerns over the outlook for the technology sector and the sustainability of the AI-driven market rally.
